_note: Base config. platform-agent-stack/setup.sh merges the chosen ITSM provider in as mcpServers.itsm - it does not edit this file in place, it backs it up first. Server names and args are the general shape; verify against the packages you actually install.
_removed: kubernetes and prometheus (npx kubernetes-mcp-server / prometheus-mcp-server) used to sit here and were unreachable: bridge/src/policy.js resolve() only ever returns backend "itsm" (from an action-mapping) or "runbook_mcp" (DIRECT_VERBS), so no verb could route to them and executor.js had no way to call them. mcpBackends.connectAll() still spawned both at every boot, where they failed on a read-only rootfs and filled the log with npm ENOENT noise that masked the real itsm failure. Holmes owns the kubernetes/prometheus toolsets anyway - see the 'Known gaps' section of bridge/README.md, and sre-investigator's toolset in swarm/swarm.config.json, which relays to Holmes rather than connecting these directly. Re-adding either means giving policy.js a way to resolve verbs to them first, not just putting the server back.
